model.rationale: The district's D+25 fundamentals, a favorable national environment for Democrats, and Haynes's overwhelming financial advantage over a nearly unfunded opponent all point the same direction, and markets price the race near 96 percent Democratic. With no polls to contradict the fundamentals, the expected margin sits in the low thirties.
model.watch: Any credible polling showing a single-digit race or large outside spending against Haynes would be the main signal that the margin is narrowing.

overview:
TX-30 is an open seat in a Dallas-area district drawn to be strongly Democratic, with a partisan lean of roughly 25 points Democratic. Frederick Haynes III, a prominent local pastor, holds a large financial advantage, raising about $420,000 with $200,000 in outside support, while Republican Everett Jackson has raised roughly $17,000 and had about $1,200 on hand. No general-election polls or expert ratings are available for this race.

Prediction markets price the Democratic nominee at around 96 percent, consistent with the district's fundamentals. The partisan baseline, the lopsided money race, and a favorable environment for Democrats all point the same way. Jackson would need a historic overperformance in a district built for Democratic strength, so the forecast expects a wide Democratic margin and classifies the race as Safe D.
